flows.title: Write a prompt that gets the image you meant
steps: Describe what you want to see in a short, clear phrase. Long lists and detailed instructions confuse the process more than they help.
Choose precise words — huge, gigantic or enormous rather than big — and give numbers, such as three cats rather than cats, or a collective noun such as a flock of birds.
Describe what you do want rather than what you do not: a prompt that mentions no cake can still produce a cake.
Name the details that matter to you — subject, medium, environment, lighting, colour, mood and composition. Fewer details give more variety and less control.
Beyond text, a prompt can carry image prompts, style references and parameters, which are added at the end of the prompt.

flows.title: Change an image you have already made
steps: Click your image on the Create or Organize page to open it and reveal the Creation Actions. If a button is missing, click More options and tick it.
Vary makes other versions of the image, subtly or strongly different; the Edit Model changes an image from plain-language instructions and reference images.
Upscale enlarges it — Creative Upscale also adds small improvements, Subtle Upscale enlarges without altering the image.
Remix iterates by changing the prompt text and parameters. The Editor holds Pan, Zoom Out and Vary Region, the erase tool, in one interface for several changes at once.
The Use buttons carry the image into a new prompt as an image prompt or style reference, or put its prompt text back in the Imagine bar; Animate turns it into a five-second video.
